title: Biomechanical Testing of Repaired Tendon
author: Susumu Yoneda
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.tadeia6

steps.title: Keep tendons wet
steps.instruction: Maintain all tendons immersed in phosphate buffered saline (PBS) throughout the entire procedure.

steps.title: Mount tendon in grips
steps.instruction: Secure the proximal tendon segment with sandpaper and a triangle‑toothed grip, secure the distal phalanx in a custom grip, and set the distance between the two grips to 60 mm.

steps.title: Apply tracking texture
steps.instruction: Apply a random texture to the tendon surface using Verhoeff’s stain to enable optical strain tracking.

steps.title: Precondition tendons
steps.instruction: Precondition each tendon by applying a preload of 1 N, then run five triangular wave cycles ranging from 0 mm to 1 mm at a displacement rate of 0.3 mm/s.

steps.title: Run tensile test to failure
steps.instruction: Place the mounted tendon on an Instron 5866 material testing machine (Norwood, MA) and pull in uniaxial tension at 0.3 mm/s until failure; record strain optically with video at 60 Hz and note the failure mode (suture pullout, suture breakage, or knot failure).

steps.title: Analyze load‑strain data
steps.instruction: Synchronize load and strain data, generate load‑displacement and load‑strain curves, and using custom MATLAB code calculate: maximum load (N), load required to create a 2 mm gap (N), stiffness (N/mm) from the linear region, strain at 20 N (%), yield force (N), and modified resilience (N·strain) as the area under the load‑strain curve up to yield; determine the 2 mm gap load by tracking displacement between points ±2 mm from the repair site.
